title: Structure-guided engineering of AI-derived adenine base editors for nuclear and mitochondrial DNA editing.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the full open-access text and its data availability statement from the cached Europe PMC copy; grepped it for every supplementary item mentioned (one file, 'gkag737_Supplemental_File'; Tables S1-S3 described as mutagenesis primers and supporting sequence information) and for all reported counts (29 endogenous nuclear loci, 32 engineered variants, 11 mutagenesis sites). Tried six download routes for the data and supplement: Europe PMC supplementaryFiles (timeout, then DNS failure), the PMC article page (403/reCAPTCHA), the Oxford University Press article page (404/DNS), and NCBI E-utilities for both BioProjects (DNS failure).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything quantitative: that editing efficiencies were measured by targeted amplicon sequencing at 29 loci across the editor panel, that only raw PCR-amplicon reads (PRJNA1415889) and RNA-seq reads (PRJNA1415900) were deposited, and that no processed per-locus or per-position efficiency table is offered. I could not open a single data file, so no row count, column name or unit was verified in a file.

a1_downloadable.note: The only deposited data is raw sequencing (PCR amplicon reads in SRA PRJNA1415889, RNA-seq in PRJNA1415900). It is public, but raw reads are explicitly out of scope for this project (never download fastq), and the processed numbers that matter exist only inside figures. The single supplement file was not retrievable in three attempts (Europe PMC timeout/DNS, PMC reCAPTCHA, publisher 404).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The label (percent adenine-to-guanine conversion per position per locus per editor) is not a column anywhere. It would have to be constructed from scratch by aligning raw amplicon reads and calling per-base conversion rates (CRISPResso2-style), i.e. rebuilding the paper's entire analysis. Supplementary Tables S1-S3 are mutagenesis primers and sequence supporting information, not a measurement table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be available in principle: the 29 target protospacer sequences and the editor protein variant sequences are described in the supplement and derive from named Addgene plasmids, but I could not open the supplement to confirm they are listed as sequences rather than locus names.

a4_units_stated.note: The paper states units clearly in prose and figure axes: editing frequency as a percentage of sequencing reads, indel frequency as a percentage. Not verified in any file because no file was obtainable.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on realistic scale. The design is 29 nuclear loci by roughly 11 editor variants, so a few hundred locus-editor measurements; even counting each adenine in the protospacer separately gives at most low thousands of values, all from one cell line (HEK293T) in one lab, with 3 replicates. Published competitors trained on 28,294-38,538 target sites. No verified count exists because no table was obtainable.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; raw amplicon FASTQ for ~300+ libraries, likely tens of GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: The processed table, if it existed, would be trivially small (well under 1 MB). But the only route to it is reprocessing raw reads, whose size I could not check (NCBI unreachable) and which plausibly exceeds the 50 MB download rule many times over.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be assessed: no file, API listing or download was retrievable, so there is nothing to compare against the paper's stated 29 loci and 32 variants.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle: editing efficiency comes from a direct physical measurement (counts of converted bases in targeted amplicon sequencing reads), not from another model's output, and it is not computable from the input sequence.

part_a_killers.note: Stopped at the first group of failures as the checklist instructs; A2 alone is fatal.

existing_models.name: BE-Hive (Arbab et al., Cell 2020), a machine-learning model of base editing outcomes
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported Pearson correlation about 0.9 for genotype outcome distribution and about 0.7 for overall efficiency, trained on 11 cytosine and adenine editors across 38,538 genomically integrated target sites; held-out target sites.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer of predictions to endogenous loci and to editor variants outside the trained panel.

existing_models.name: BE-DICT (Marquart et al., Nature Communications 2021), an attention-based deep learning predictor
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on 28,294 lentivirally integrated target sequences for adenine and cytosine editors; reported high per-base accuracy on held-out library sequences and endogenous validation sites.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation across cell types and to new editor architectures.

existing_models.name: DeepABE / DeepBaseEditor (Song et al.; Kim group), convolutional neural network predictors of editing efficiency and outcome
existing_models.score_and_split: Convolutional network trained on large target-library screens; published correlations in the 0.7-0.9 range on held-out library targets, with a web tool.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Prediction for newly engineered deaminase variants not in the training panel.

existing_models.name: BEDICT2.0 (Genome Biology 2025), deep learning for adenine base editing efficiency across cellular contexts
existing_models.score_and_split: Correlation R = 0.60-0.94 in cell lines and R = 0.62-0.81 in mouse liver, trained on screens of 2,195 pathogenic mutations with about 12,000 guide RNAs for SpRY-ABEmax and SpRY-ABE8e.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Extending predictions to additional editor variants and tissues beyond those screened.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or DNABERT-2 for the 20-nucleotide protospacer, with ESM-2 embeddings of the deaminase variant
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would suffice for a few thousand short sequences
backbone.licence: Nucleotide Transformer and ESM-2 weights are openly downloadable; not the limiting factor here

integration.partner_dataset: BE-Hive and BE-DICT training libraries, plus Be-dataHIVE (a public base-editing database)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do efficiency models trained on library screens of older editors transfer to newly engineered deaminase variants such as OpenABE, or does each new editor need its own screen? — a good question, but it needs this paper's per-position efficiencies as a table, which the paper does not provide.

controls.positive_control: ABE8e, included in the paper's panel as the field-standard editor, whose per-position efficiency profile is already well characterised and should be recovered by any working model.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle editor labels across loci and confirm performance collapses to the per-locus mean.
controls.external_validation: BE-Hive or BEDICT2.0 predictions on the same 29 protospacers, or the published library screens as a second independent source.

honest_claim_h3: At best this paper could support: 'for 29 protospacers in one human cell line, a model ranks which adenine positions a given engineered deaminase edits' — but the per-position numbers exist only inside the paper's figures, so even that claim cannot be made without reprocessing raw sequencing reads.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use target DNA sequence and base-editor protein variant to predict how often each adenine gets converted to guanine.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one target site, one editor variant and one adenine position within it: the 20-letter target sequence plus a representation of the deaminase protein. The paper's design gives 29 target sites across roughly 11 editors, so a few hundred site-editor pairs; no verified row count exists because no data table is available.
plain_idea.predict: The percentage of sequencing reads in which that adenine was read as guanine, measured by PCR amplification of the target region followed by deep sequencing in HEK293T human cells, three biological replicates.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Gene-editing labs choose a guide and an editor before spending weeks on an experiment, so a predictor of which positions get edited saves real bench time. Here the value is mostly hypothetical, because the measurements are not released in usable form.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes 29 target loci in one cell line; BE-Hive trained on 38,538 target sites, BE-DICT on 28,294, and BEDICT2.0 on about 12,000 guide RNAs across cell lines and mouse liver. The only novel slice is the new OpenABE variants themselves, and that slice is far too small to train on.

confidence_score.why: Three biological replicates per point would allow a noise estimate, but the replicate-level values are not released, and with a few hundred points there is no room to calibrate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: BEDICT2.0 is a 2025 model evaluated across held-out cell lines and in vivo liver (R = 0.60-0.94), with code and a web tool; BE-Hive (2020) and BE-DICT (2021) are open and were evaluated on held-out targets. Open, recent and honestly evaluated is the combination the checklist calls fatal.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first and third conditions: our model could not see what theirs sees (we have no training table at all), and the paper's endogenous-locus amplicon assay is not the same measurement as their integrated-library screens, so adding it would mix assays rather than extend one.

ml_idea: The project considered was: predict per-adenine A-to-G conversion efficiency from the target protospacer sequence plus an embedding of the deaminase variant, and test whether published predictors (BE-Hive, BE-DICT, BEDICT2.0) transfer to newly engineered editors. The transfer question is genuinely good and cannot produce a useless answer, but this paper supplies no table to test it on.

effort.compute_note: The modelling itself would be trivial on a laptop (a few hundred to few thousand short sequences). The 40 hours is the cost of rebuilding the labels from raw amplicon reads with read alignment and per-base conversion calling, plus curating 29 target and 11 protein sequences by hand; all figures are estimates, nothing was timed because no data was obtained.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the single supplement file (gkag737_Supplemental_File) and look for a table of per-locus editing percentages. If it contains only primer and guide sequences, as the in-text citations suggest, the project is dead and no further work is justified.

verdict_reason: Fails A2, the checklist's most common killer: the prediction target (percent adenine-to-guanine conversion per position) is not a column anywhere, only a figure, so it would have to be reconstructed from raw amplicon sequencing reads in SRA — exactly the raw-data reprocessing this project excludes. Scale fails too (29 target loci, one cell line, one lab; at most low thousands of position-level values against competitors' 28,000-38,500 target sites), and the field is saturated with open, recently and honestly evaluated models (BE-Hive, BE-DICT, DeepABE, BEDICT2.0). Note the limitation on my side: the supplement was unreachable through all three routes, so A2 rests on the paper's own description of Tables S1-S3 as primer and sequence information rather than on opening the file; the cheapest check is to open that file if network access returns.
